intelligence.human_view: Think of a body. Your heart doesn't keep its own separate diary, your lungs don't file their own paperwork — one blood flow runs through organs that each do their one job, and the medical chart records how the whole person is doing. This family is NayaNET deciding to be a body instead of a drawer of parts — and being honest about which organ is still healing.
intelligence.simple_view: When you finish a puzzle, you don't just say 'done' — you show the picture, you point to the one piece that's still missing under the couch, and you let Mum look. That's how people know your 'done' means something next time too.
intelligence.grandma_view: A family is like that too: one family, shared table, shared stories — and still, you don't open your sister's letters. Togetherness was never the same as no boundaries. It's good to see a computer system finally written that way round.
intelligence.naya_view: Close the current unit with its proof before opening the next. Never batch claims about live state inside a propagation window. Build hero lists from recorded pains. Capture the note at the moment of learning, not at the end of the day.
